statement: Build a singly linked list from the given values, reverse it by rewiring the next pointers - no copying values into an array - and print the reversed chain on one line, separated by single spaces. Walk the chain once, turning each arrow backwards as you pass.

example.why: Each node ends up pointing at its former predecessor, and the old tail becomes the head.

hint: Three names run the loop: previous, current and a saved next. Save next before turning the arrow.
mistake: Turning current.next before saving it - the rest of the chain becomes unreachable on the spot.

tests.note: single node is its own reverse
